newsitem.title: INDIA: India "Bandit Queen" to come out of hiding.
newsitem.headline: India "Bandit Queen" to come out of hiding.

text.p: Former "Bandit Queen" Phoolan Devi -- a fugitive once again after old charges against her were revived -- will come out of hiding to face the courts and do her duty as a member of the Indian parliament, her lawyer said on Wednesday.

"Such a move was necessitated in view of the commencement of the budget session tomorrow which by virtue of being a people's representative, she is expected to attend," lawyer Nand Lal Jaiswal told Reuters by telephone in Lucknow, capital of the northern state of Uttar Pradesh.
Devi was portrayed in the film "Bandit Queen" as a rape victim from a low caste community of boatmen whose career of crime began as a search for revenge on her attackers.

She shot to notoriety in 1981 when 22 upper caste men were massacred in the northern Indian village of Behmai. She denied leading the killers but surrendered to police in the central state of Madhya Pradesh in 1983.

When she was released on parole in 1994 other charges against her in Uttar Pradesh were dropped. She joined a regional party which represents low castes and won a parliamentary seat in last year's general elections.
The Uttar Pradesh high court revived charges against her this month at the request of a man who says he was one of her intended victims.
She faces a total of 57 counts including murder. Police issued a nationwide alert and searched two of her homes but failed to find her.
